page.layout: One printed title page on the scan. Top: title in spaced capitals, with the author's name in larger type, then a block of roman lines in full width. Below: an italic verse of three lines, centred. Middle: a woodcut device with a circular motto. Foot: a centred imprint in spaced capitals. A handwritten "5" sits at the top right corner, outside the printed page.

main_text.l: Ad capiendum, deplumandum & dilacerandum audaciorem illum Cuculum Ubiquitarium, qui nuper ex
Iacobi Andreæ, mali corui, malo ouo, ab Holdero,
simplicissima Curruca exclusus, & à Dæmonico Bauio Fescennio varij coloris plumis instructus, impetum in Philomelas innocentes facere cœperat.

l.i: Dum Cuculus nimium confidit viribus, atq;
Argutas acer dum petit hostis aues;
Ecce illum pedibus comprensum euiscerat uncis
Falco, his urbs misit quem Tigurina locis.

page.notes: The handwritten "5" at the top right is not printed and is left out. The text is clear throughout. Two spellings were normalised for u/v: "Vbiquitarium" to "Ubiquitarium", "vncis" to "uncis", and "VS" to "US" in EMISSUS, TIGU-, BEUMLERO and NEOSTADII PALATINORUM. The woodcut device shows an oval with a motto in a ring and a central emblem of hands holding a cornucopia under a radiant sun. The motto ring is hard to read at its bottom, so "DITAT" is marked [?]. The verse is set in italic, and the initial letters of the verse are decorative.
